venues.scale_description: Ice arena opened to the public 16 March 2007, replacing the original Altrincham Ice Rink which closed in 2003. Was the 2025-26 Elite Ice Hockey League home of Manchester Storm, but the same evidence records that Storm departed in April 2026 to relocate to the AO Arena; remaining tenants are Altrincham Aces, Manchester Metros (university) and the Manchester Storm junior academy. It therefore remains a >=1,000-capacity spectator ice arena with a continuing hockey programme, but its EIHL status has ended and that should be re-checked before any EIHL-derived assumption is made about it.

evidence.note: Establishes the full address and postcode (Oakfield Road, Altrincham WA14 1BA), the 2,140 seated / up to 300 standing capacity, the 2,351 record sell-out attendance, the 16 March 2007 opening, operator Planet Ice, and critically that Manchester Storm left for the AO Arena in April 2026.

Reference population for the ice-hockey cross-check: the ten 2025-26 EIHL venues and capacities. Nine of the ten (SSE Arena Belfast, Vindico Arena, Planet Ice Coventry/SkyDome, Dundee Ice Arena, Fife Ice Arena, Braehead Arena, Guildford Spectrum, Motorpoint Arena Nottingham, Utilita Arena Sheffield) already reconcile to existing census records; Planet Ice Altrincham (listed at 2,440) was the only one missing.

Operator site checked for an Altrincham-specific fixture calendar; it lists the 14-venue Planet Ice estate and group-wide dated events but no per-venue Altrincham calendar, which is why no calendar source is asserted.

CORRECTION 1 - STALE NAME. The infobox gives the current name as "Club Doncaster Sports Village", with former names "Keepmoat Stadium (November 2006-December 2021)" and "Eco-Power Stadium (December 2021-May 2026)". The census holds this venue under the name it lost in 2021. CORRECTION 2 - MISCLASSIFICATION. The census records it as venue_type RUGBY_STADIUM; the infobox gives owner and operator as Doncaster Rovers Football Club, with football tenants Doncaster Rovers (2007-present) and Doncaster Rovers Belles, and rugby league tenants Doncaster R.L.F.C. and Sheffield Eagles (2015, 2021). It is primarily a football stadium and is reclassified FOOTBALL_STADIUM here. CORRECTION 3 - ADDRESS/CAPACITY. Address "Stadium Way, Lakeside, Doncaster, South Yorkshire, England DN4 5JW"; capacity 15,231. The census record carried null operator, null official_url and no address.

CORRECTION 4 - DUPLICATE. Confirms Doncaster Knights (rugby union) play at Armthorpe Road / Castle Park, i.e. a different Doncaster ground, so the census's RUGBY_STADIUM classification of the Keepmoat is not explained by a rugby union tenancy. Read together with the census's own separate FOOTBALL_STADIUM record "Club Doncaster Sports Village" (city Doncaster, operator "Doncaster Rovers F.C."), the census holds the SAME physical stadium twice under two different names and two different venue_types. These two records must be merged.

venues.scale_description: CORRECTION TO EXISTING CENSUS RECORD - RECLASSIFICATION, NOT CLOSURE. Greyhound racing at this site (branded Suffolk Downs during part of its second spell) ceased on 2 April 2026, ending its second spell; the venue is no longer one of GBGB's 16 licensed tracks, so the census's GREYHOUND_STADIUM classification is now wrong. However the SITE IS NOT CLOSED: it opened in May 1975 for speedway, Spedeworth International owns the land, and speedway (Sundays, April-October) and stock-car racing continue. It is therefore re-typed OTHER_SPORTS_VENUE and left OPERATIONAL - it would be equally wrong to mark a live motorsport venue CLOSED as to leave a defunct greyhound track listed as an active one. Its greyhound history: racing began 21 September 1991, ceased 15 January 2018, resumed 8 February 2022, and ended 2 April 2026, with a significant fire on 30 July 2024 destroying a machinery building and damaging the bar and offices. No spectator capacity figure was found on any page fetched, so capacity is left null rather than guessed.

evidence.note: Trade-press openings/closures register (current as at 24 July 2026) recording 'April 2nd, 2026 SUFFOLK DOWNS (aka MILDENHALL) (closure of second spell)' and the corresponding 'February 2nd, 2022 SUFFOLK DOWNS (aka MILDENHALL - opens for second spell)'.
